title: bug: local runner compares its own projectPath unresolved, so a native alias (//x on POSIX, /x on Windows) refuses its own daemon
description: scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs loopbackDaemonHost and vm-control.mjs readDaemonInfo compare canonicalProjectPath(own) without path.resolve, and runner-client.mjs discover uses an exact `info.projectPath !== projectPath`. A native alias of the project therefore reads its own daemon as foreign. That is the same class as task-f33bf7af's proxy and doctor fix (non-destructive refusal; callers usually pass canonical paths). guest-session.mjs:82 also still names the twin as index.ts; the twin now lives in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/projectPath.ts (index.ts re-exports it). Confirm first whether runner-client's exact match is deliberate.

These are guards: they pass on HEAD, and they kill a fix that calls canonicalProjectPath before the typeof check, which would surface a raw TypeError instead of a RUNNER_* code.
  - Keep 'another project' as it is.
- New C2 row (R1), next to "hashes daemon.json's projectPath": 'admits this project recorded in another spelling and reads the key filed under it'.

- C4-C9 before(): start the real daemon with `init --project spelled(project)`. File every key under keyName(spelled(project)): the sentinel write, the 'daemon reused the sentinel key' read-back, and C6's wrong key. The client keeps passing `project`.

  - Do NOT use //x for the real daemon on POSIX: the daemon's own isForeignDaemonInfo treats //x as foreign, so `stop --project` would refuse it.

scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs:
(a) loopbackDaemonHost gets one more option: `{ timeoutMs = 5_000, signal, spelling } = {}`.
- It admits only when `(spelling === undefined || report.projectPath === spelling)` also holds, next to the existing healthy, canonical-project and loopback-bind checks.
- Add one sentence to its doc comment: with spelling, the report must also name the project exactly so, because runner-client reads the key filed under that string.
- daemonRefusal and vm-control's readDaemonInfo pass no spelling, so their rule is unchanged. VC-M2 pins that vm-control still admits a daemon.json spelled unlike its report.
(b) In the canonicalProjectPath doc comment (~line 82), the daemon twin is packages/moe-daemon/src/util/projectPath.ts (index.ts re-exports it). Change nothing else there.
Do NOT change canonicalProjectPath's code or output. It is also ownedLedgerDir's hash input, and VC-L2 pins the ledger keys.

scripts/local-runner/runner-client.mjs:
- Import canonicalProjectPath from './guest-session.mjs', which runner-client already imports from.
- discover() refuses RUNNER_DAEMON_INFO_INVALID when `!isRecord(info) || typeof info.projectPath !== 'string' || canonicalProjectPath(info.projectPath) !== canonicalProjectPath(projectPath)`, or on a bad port.
- Then call loopbackDaemonHost(info, projectPath, { timeoutMs, signal, spelling: info.projectPath }).
- runnerKeyFile(info.projectPath) stays unchanged; that spelling is now the one the daemon itself reported.
- Update the header comment and the discover() comment, briefly:
  - daemon.json may record this project in another spelling. JetBrains records D:/x on Windows while path.resolve gives D:\x, so the old exact match refused every caller there.
  - The key is the one runnerKeyPath filed under that recorded spelling.
  - The daemon's own report must repeat that spelling byte for byte, so daemon.json still only refuses.

Error handling:
- Keep the typeof check before canonicalProjectPath. canonicalProjectPath trims, so a non-string would throw a raw TypeError that escapes discover() uncoded.
- Every refusal stays exactly one fixed RUNNER_* code in the fixed message: INFO_INVALID for daemon.json, NOT_LOOPBACK when the daemon's own report does not admit (including a spelling mismatch), ABORTED for the signal.
- No path, key byte or upstream text goes into any error.
- loopbackDaemonHost still never rejects; it resolves null on every failure.

Step 1's RED rows go GREEN; every other row is unchanged.

comments.author: architect-4ff0711c
comments.content:
Planner findings (architect-4ff0711c), written before the plan.

1. The title's premise does not hold for guest-session.mjs or vm-control.mjs.
- Their canonicalProjectPath already applies path.resolve to its argument, so '//x' on Linux and '/x' on native Windows (cwd drive) both reduce to the canonical spelling. I probed this with Linux node and with node.exe.
- DB1 and VC-M2 already pin other spellings of the caller's own path.
- No logic change there. The plan adds a guard row, DB6, using the title's exact aliases.

2. The runner-client exact match: deliberate as written, wrong as an identity rule.
- CQ-V04b1's plan chose `projectPath === path.resolve(input)`.
- The daemon records --project exactly as given. daemon.json, the /health projectPath and runnerKeyPath all use that raw string.
- JetBrains passes basePath with forward slashes. The live .moe/daemon.json says 'D:/projexts/moes', but path.resolve always yields 'D:\projexts\moes'.
- So on native Windows, openRunnerChannel refuses with RUNNER_DAEMON_INFO_INVALID for every caller spelling. Probed with node.exe.
- The exact match also stopped daemon.json from choosing the key file, since the key is filed under sha256 of the daemon's spelling. The plan keeps that. daemon.json may name the project in any canonical-equal spelling, and the key is the one filed under that spelling. But the daemon's own /health report must repeat that spelling byte for byte, so daemon.json can still only refuse.

3. Line 82: the comment fix is in the plan.

Residual, out of scope:
- The local canonicalProjectPath also resolves the reported path and has no //wsl$ mapping. Across the WSL boundary it can therefore differ from the daemon contract. For example, on win32 a report of '/home/x' reads as '<drive>:\home\x'.
- It is also ownedLedgerDir's hash input, so changing it would move VM ledgers. Left unchanged.

Error handling is unchanged: every refusal is one fixed RUNNER_* code. guest-session (daemonRefusal) and vm-control (readDaemonInfo) keep their rule; a guard row shows all three modules already admit the caller's native alias (//x on POSIX, /x on win32). The guest-session canonicalProjectPath comment names packages/moe-daemon/src/util/projectPath.ts as the daemon twin.

R2: daemon.json names spelled(project) while /health names project. Result: RUNNER_DAEMON_NOT_LOOPBACK, no socket and no key read. Fails on HEAD with RUNNER_DAEMON_INFO_INVALID.

DB6: guest-session, runner-client and vm-control each admit their own daemon when the caller spells the project //x (POSIX) or /x (win32). Passes on HEAD and after the change.
VC-M2, DB1-DB5, the bridge tests and every other existing row pass unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Keep the exact match and only fix comments. Rejected: the runner channel stays unusable on native Windows whenever JetBrains started the daemon (forward-slash basePath), whatever the caller's spelling.
2. Relax to canonical equality and keep hashing daemon.json's spelling. Rejected: daemon.json would then choose which same-project key file is read, including a relative spelling that resolves differently from the daemon's own cwd. That breaks the 'daemon.json can only refuse' invariant this file and the daemon-bind tests state.
3. CHOSEN: canonical equality, plus the daemon's own /health report must repeat daemon.json's spelling byte for byte, via an optional `spelling` on loopbackDaemonHost.
4. Make the daemon canonicalize --project. Rejected: it moves every runner key (a new runnerId) and changes daemon.json for every consumer; too large for a LOW row.
5. Port the daemon's comparableProjectPath into the local runner. Rejected: it changes canonicalProjectPath's output, which moves ownedLedgerDir and orphans recorded VMs, and the stated bug does not need it.

- runner-client already hashes info.projectPath (CQ-V04b1: 'the client must hash daemon.json's projectPath, not the caller's spelling'). The exact match made that moot.
- Existing guards: DB1 'this project in another spelling', VC-M2 (in vm-control, a daemon.json spelled unlike the report is admitted) and VC-L2 (ledger keys).

- Real daemon on POSIX: use a trailing slash, never //x. The daemon's isForeignDaemonInfo reads //x as foreign, so `stop --project <canonical>` would refuse it. A trailing slash and forward slashes compare equal via comparableProjectPath.
- The shared dist is stale (no /health bind report), so C4-C9 are meaningful only in the snapshot.
